summary: How-to for playing a Level Sequence cutscene from gameplay: a Trigger Box overlap in the Level Blueprint calls Play on the sequence player, Set Playback Position rewinds it for replays, and an F key skip uses Go to End and Stop so end-state changes still apply.
gotchas: A sequence played with Play only runs once; call Set Playback Position to 0 before Play to replay it
Stop halts mid-sequence and leaves partial state; Go to End and Stop applies the final state when skipping
Set the track's When Finished to Keep State for changes to persist after the sequence ends

summary: Python scripting guide for Movie Render Graph: creating a graph config, overriding user-exposed graph variables on a queue job, editing Global Output Settings node defaults, traversing graph nodes and scripting comment boxes, with example scripts shipped in the MovieRenderPipeline plugin.
gotchas: Reporting an error does not finish the executor; custom executors must call on_executor_finished_impl() when done, including after a fatal error
Executor finished callback receives success = False if any job had a fatal error
Graph created by the script has entangled node layout that must be moved apart manually

summary: Python reference for Sequencer: loading, creating, opening and focusing Level Sequences, setting frame rate and playback range, adding actors as possessables or spawnables, creating cameras, adding tracks and sections (transform, skeletal animation), copy/paste of folders, bindings, tracks and sections, and track filters.
gotchas: Call refresh_current_level_sequence() to see newly added tracks and sections in the UI
Animation track sections need params.animation set to an animation asset before they do anything
Spawnables are made by adding actors as possessables first and then converting

summary: Short how-to for Take Recorder with Live Link (Face AR Sample): adding an actor source, recording and reviewing takes, changing the take save location, and layered take recording to stack several actors' performances in one sequence.
keys: Start a new recording using this Take as base
gotchas: Requires the Take Recorder plugin to be enabled
Default take save location is Cinematics > Takes

summary: Shows how to render several Cine Camera angles from one shot with Movie Render Queue by adding a Camera setting with Render All Cameras and using the {camera_name} format string in output paths.
gotchas: Movie Render Queue plugin must be enabled and the editor restarted
If {camera_name} is not used, MRQ appends the camera name as a suffix to avoid file name conflicts
Duplicate camera names are auto-renamed by MRQ

summary: Legacy guide to Sequencer's Render Movie option for capturing a sequence to an AVI video or image sequence, with optional burn-ins; the feature is deprecated in favour of Movie Render Queue.
gotchas: Deprecated since Unreal Engine 5.0
Clicking Cancel at the save prompt aborts the render

summary: How-to for embedding a sequence inside an Actor Blueprint with the Actor Sequence Component, editing it in the Blueprint's Sequencer tab, auto-playing or looping it, and playing it from the Event Graph through the component's Sequence Player.
gotchas: Experimental feature; may not work as expected or may change
Requires enabling the Actor Sequence Editor plugin and restarting the editor

summary: Overview of the Sequencer Editor UI: toolbar buttons, outliner, timeline navigation and zoom, playhead scrubbing, selection ranges, custom frame marks (including determinism fences), playback controls, and media track scrubbing and looping behaviour.
gotchas: Only one custom mark can exist per frame
H.264/5 media scrubs with a few frames of lag; Apple ProRes scrubs best
Synchronous Scrubbing affects only scrubbing, not playback
Asterisk on playhead time means a sub-frame position, which happens when snapping is disabled

summary: Reference table of Sequencer keyboard shortcuts for playback and timing, timeline navigation, keyframing, interpolation mode keys 1-5, section split/trim, and transform keying (S, Shift+W/E/R).

Explains the Playlists virtual-production panel for preparing a list of Level Sequences and triggering them as subsequences on demand, usually during a Take Recorder session, with hold, loop, offset, mute and Play All controls.
gotchas: Playlists plugin (Virtual Production section) must be enabled and the editor restarted
Hold works by creating a second instance of the sequence with Time Scale 0

summary: Lists Sequencer track types and how to add actors and component tracks, rename, lock, pin, mute, solo, reorder, search and filter tracks, and add track conditions (group, platform, scalability or custom Blueprint/Director conditions).
gotchas: Only one track can be pinned per sequence
Mute and Solo are editor-only and do not affect the level at runtime except during Play In Editor
Muting an Object Binding Track also hides the actor in the viewport
Conditions work by default for sections converted to ECS

summary: Covers building cinematics from Level Sequences, Shots and Takes: Add Level Sequence with Shots settings, the Shots track, shot properties, metadata, origin overrides, time warp, thumbnails, sequence context, Hierarchical Bias for resolving actor conflicts between nested sequences, and creating and switching Takes.
gotchas: Overlapping shots on higher tracks take priority over lower tracks
Default Hierarchical Bias is 0 for root and 100 per subsequence level, compounding, so the deepest sequence wins; equal bias blends values

summary: Tour of the Slay virtual-production sample from Fab: opening the TF_Edit master sequence, shot-based workflow with level visibility, spawnables, lighting/FX subscenes, lighting channels, material parameter tracks, post-process ray tracing, and its Movie Render Queue preset and cvars.
gotchas: Requires at least an Intel Core i9 and GeForce RTX 2080 Ti or similar
Long initial load as assets compile the first time
Sample appears in Fab Library only when the compatible engine version is installed

summary: Explains Possessable versus Spawnable bindings in Sequencer, how to create or convert spawnables, and the Spawnable properties such as Spawned Object Owner, Spawnable Level, Continuously Respawn and Convert to Possessable, with temporary per-shot lights as the example use.
gotchas: Spawnable Level cannot target World Partition or Data Layers
Change Class keeps Sequencer tracks but not non-Sequencer object properties
External owner spawns but never destroys the actor; destroy it yourself via Sequencer Tags and Groups

summary: Full reference for Take Recorder: recording gameplay, cameras, Live Link, microphone audio, player and world sources into Sequencer, with toolbar, slate, source options, presets, project/user settings (clock source, save dirs, possessable vs spawnable), timecode recording and unlocking takes for editing.
gotchas: Requires the Take Recorder plugin (Live Link plugin optional for mocap)
Only properties that have a recorder and a keyframeable Sequencer track can be recorded
Particles from Spawn Emitter functions are only captured with the World source
Auto Serialize is experimental and not fully tested

summary: Maps Movie Render Queue config settings to their Movie Render Graph nodes (File Type Output, Sampling Method, Renderer, Warm Up, Debug Settings, Game Overrides, Path Tracer vs Deferred) and lists MRQ features MRG does not yet support.
gotchas: MRG does not yet support nDisplay rendering, High Resolution rendering, Apple ProRes plugin, Final Cut Pro XML, Prestreaming Recorder or 32 Bit Post Process Material rendering
Deleting or disconnecting the Game Overrides node removes its effect, unlike the MRQ config

summary: Step-by-step setup for firing Level Blueprint logic from a Sequencer Event Track by implementing a shared Blueprint Interface in both the Level Blueprint and the sequence Director Blueprint and binding the event key's Pass Bound Object To to Target.
gotchas: The interface function call must target the Sequence Director BP; other targets will not work
Pass Bound Object To must be set to Target even with no real target, so the interface falls back to the Level Blueprint

summary: Describes launching Movie Render Queue renders from the command line with a Level Sequence plus primary config, a saved queue asset, or a custom Python executor class, with example UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe lines.
gotchas: C++ referencing MoviePipelineMasterConfig.h must switch to MovePipelinePrimaryConfig.h
Smallest distributable unit is one camera cut/shot, not a frame
-LevelSequence mode renders a single job on a single map
Custom Python executors need an init_unreal.py in /Content/Python importing the module

summary: Hub page for the Virtual Camera system (VCamComponent with Modifiers and Output Providers driving a Cine Camera), linking to Live Link control, Unreal VCam app tools and settings, multi-user setup, component configuration, inputs and multiple cameras.

How-to for choosing per track whether Sequencer changes persist or revert when a sequence finishes, using the When Finished property (Keep State vs Restore State), and how the Level Sequence Actor's global Restore State overrides it.
gotchas: Restore State on the Level Sequence Actor overrides per-track Keep State; disable it to keep changes
Default When Finished value is Restore State

summary: Overview of animating Control Rigs in Sequencer: adding a rig to a Skeletal Mesh track, keying controls, showing multiple rigs, and Layered Control Rig tracks with Order and Weight for layering edits over animation sequences.
gotchas: Layered Control Rig tracks require a working Backwards Solve graph
Tracks evaluate in descending Order (default 100); a non-layered track with lower order can clobber layered results
Ctrl+G reverts selected keys to default; Ctrl+I zeroes them

summary: Explains animation constraints in Animation Mode (Translation, Rotation, Scale, Parent, LookAt) for attaching controls or actors without reparenting, including compensating keys, priority order, baking to keys, Dynamic Offset, Maintain Offset and the Constraints Manager actor.
gotchas: Requires Animation Mode to be enabled
Constraints lower in the list take priority over earlier ones on the same channels
Parent Constraint excludes scale unless Scaling is enabled
Compensate Key needs the playhead on the constraint keyframe being fixed

summary: Describes Control Rig graph debugging: Debug/Release mode toggle, breakpoints and step controls, watching pin values, Show Node Run Counts, VM profiling of node execution time, and the Execution Stack panel.
gotchas: While stopped at breakpoints time does not advance, so accumulated time nodes do not change
Adding a breakpoint auto-enables Debug Mode

summary: Explains Control Rig solve directions: Forwards Solve (controls drive bones), Backwards Solve (bones drive controls, used for Bake To Control Rig in Sequencer), Construction Event for initialization and spawning rig elements, and the Backwards and Forwards preview mode.
keys: Import Anim Sequence Into This Sequence
gotchas: A rig without a Backwards Solve node is not selectable in Bake To Control Rig
Spawn nodes only work in the Construction Event
Spawned element count limit defaults to 128 (Procedural Element Limit)
Spawned elements' initial values are read-only in Details and must be set on the node

summary: How to build a Full Body IK node in Control Rig for procedural adjustments like ground alignment or reaching: root bone, effectors tied to controls, bone settings (stiffness, preferred angles, limits), excluded bones, and a full node pin reference.
gotchas: Requires the FullBodyIK plugin and an editor restart
Higher Iterations increase CPU cost; stiffness, mass and limits slow convergence
Excluding bones is recommended over making them fully stiff or locked

summary: Shows how to make project-wide Control Rig function libraries by creating a skeleton-free Control Rig asset with Public functions, referencing or localizing them in other rigs, and where to find the engine StandardFunctionLibrary.
gotchas: Edits to the engine StandardFunctionLibrary are lost on engine reinstall/update; make your own library instead
Custom functions can only live inside Control Rig assets

summary: Explains using the Control Rig node in an Animation Blueprint's Anim Graph to drive a rig procedurally (for example ground alignment), its pose-transfer properties, and exposing rig variables or control transforms as pins or driving floats with anim curves.
gotchas: Variables must be made instance-editable (eye icon) before they can be exposed as pins
Disabling Transfer Pose in Global Space can improve performance; results only differ if skeleton hierarchies differ

summary: Covers the Control Rig Component for driving Control Rigs from Actor Blueprint gameplay logic: setup and mapping to a Skeletal Mesh in On Pre Initialize, component details like lazy evaluation, its init/setup/solve events, and mapping other components to rig elements via details or graph nodes.
keys: Add Mapped Skeletal Mesh Bone Array
gotchas: The Skeletal Mesh must be mapped in the On Pre Initialize event
Add Mapped Skeletal Mesh Bone Array maps only listed bones/curves; follow with Add Mapped Skeletal Mesh to map the whole skeleton

summary: Explains storing rig element poses in Rig Pose variables with Get Pose Cache and applying them with Apply Pose Cache, plus the other pose cache nodes and their Element Type, Space and Items to Set options.
gotchas: If Items to Set is empty, all elements of the chosen Element Type are included

summary: Python scripting for Control Rig: modules and graph terminology, loading or creating ControlRigBlueprint assets, the Control Rig Python Log and Run Python Context, Copy Python Script, adding unit nodes, editing the hierarchy, variables, preview mesh, recompiling, and the plugin's init_unreal.py startup scripts.
gotchas: Load the ControlRigDeveloper module first with unreal.load_module before editing rigs
Rig elements are structs copied by value; after changing one you may need to set it back in the hierarchy
Python Editor Script Plugin is a dependency auto-enabled with Control Rig

summary: How to rig long chains (tails, tentacles, spines) in Control Rig with Spline From Points driven by controls and Fit Chain on Spline Curve to drive bones, with property tables and the list of spline nodes.
gotchas: A spline needs at least four points
Point and bone array order must match the spline direction
Higher sample counts increase performance cost

summary: Shows how to change a control's shape and color, and how to edit or replace the Control Shape Library (ControlRigGizmoLibrary) including importing custom FBX static meshes as new shapes.
gotchas: Default library lives in Engine > Plugins > Control Rig Content > Controls; enable engine and plugin content to see it
When importing shape meshes disable Import Textures and set Material Import Method to Do Not Create Material

summary: Reference for Control Rig elements: creating and parenting Controls, Bones and Nulls, Add Controls For Selected, control Animation Types and Value Types, transform limits, editing initial poses via Setup Event, and the Initial, Current and Offset transform types.
gotchas: Float, Integer and Vector 2D controls are limited to 0-100 by default
Bool controls are not visible in the viewport
Current pose edits in the Control Rig editor are temporary and reset on recompile or reopen
Offset only exists on Euler Transform controls
